extraction.body: Binance has suffered the biggest hack in crypto history , but that's done little to shake confidence in bitcoin , according to market analysts and researchers. On Thursday, the world's largest exchange by daily trading volume said that roughly $6.3 billion were affected in an exploit. Security firm TRM Labs linked the security incident to North Korea. The hack sparked a slight sell-off in bitcoin . On Friday, the cryptocurrency traded at $77,065 around 1:34 p.m. ET, down about 4% on the day. By comparison, the token has fallen 8.3% on average in the first 24 hours following past crypto exchange exploits, according to data from institutional crypto platform Anchorage Digital. The digital asset has remained relatively resilient because the hack on Binance had nothing to do with the security of the bitcoin network itself, according to Sam Callahan, director of bitcoin strategy and research at crypto treasury firm OranjeBTC. "Investors recognize an important distinction: Bitcoin itself was not hacked," Callahan told CNBC. "This was a security breach at a centralized exchange, not a failure of the Bitcoin network." Although Binance has suffered the largest hack in crypto history, it's far from the only digital asset exchange to fall victim to bad actors and lead bitcoin to tumble. In the early 2010s, bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox was hacked a handful of times, wreaking havoc on the price of bitcoin. The token fell as much as 23.7% in the first 24 hours after an attack on Mt. Gox in February 2014, per Anchorage Digital data. More recently, crypto exchange Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to an exploit targeting its trading platform. Last month, crypto platform Bitget was drained of more than $350 million in digital assets. What's different about the Binance hack is that it hasn't sparked the same loss in confidence in crypto markets that occurred after other major crypto security incidents, according to Spencer Hallarn, head of markets at crypto trading firm GSR. Binance said it has started recovering affected assets, which has likely assuaged some of investors' concerns, according to Spencer Hallarn, head of markets at crypto trading firm GSR. "The speed of Binance's response, its deep financial resources, and its assurances that no user funds would be lost have helped restore market confidence and prevent potential panic," Hallarn told CNBC. Tether, Circle and several other crypto firms said they had frozen roughly $3 billion in funds stolen in the heist. That should help mitigate losses tied to the attack, the executive noted. Binance also has a $1.2 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users to offset losses from security breaches and other events. The firm could also be eligible for loans that would minimize its solvency risks, if history is any indication, according to investment bank Compass Point. "We believe Binance has more than enough liquidity to cover the hole and we expect the exchange to remain solvent while reimbursing user funds," Compass Point analyst Ed Engel said Friday in a note to clients. "ByBit also received a bridge loan after its $1.5bn hack last year; therefore, we believe Binance has financing options." GSR's Hallarn noted that this latest rotation out of technology stocks may also be to blame for some of the pressure on bitcoin. "Since the exploit, bitcoin has largely traded in lockstep with other risk assets, including equities, which sold off overnight amid concerns over AI-related earnings," Hallarn told CNBC. The iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) was down more than 8% on the day. Still, Anchorage Digital head of research David Lawant noted that current holders of bitcoin are more likely to hold their tokens through short-term headwinds than holders of other risk-on assets at the moment. Just 6% of bitcoin is held in exchange-traded funds, according to data from bitcoin analytics platform Bitbo. That suggests many bitcoins are still being held by long-term believers in the asset and its cypherpunk origins, Lawant said. "Bitcoin and crypto are not these hot-topic [assets like tech stocks] that investors are fleeing in and out," Lawant said. "The current holder base is a pretty strong one that is able to look at these things with a slightly longer-term view. That's playing a big role in how bitcoin is behaving well in this negative market environment." extraction.body: Cole's comments came in an interview on Cointelegraph 's Chain Reaction on Friday. During the aftermath of the hack, Bitcoin traded around $77,400 as of Saturday at 4:00 pm, according to CoinGecko price data-about 4% below its level shortly before the Thursday incident began. Cole said the scale of the Binance breach had not changed his long-term view of Bitcoin. In his framing, the attack resembles a bank robbery-something that can happen to a particular institution-rather than evidence that the broader financial system has stopped working. He also suggested the market decline was less severe than he expected given both the magnitude of the hack and wider weakness across crypto markets. At the same time, Cole acknowledged that it was too early to determine whether Bitcoin had reached a durable price bottom. Looking ahead, Cole described the market as being in an“early spring” recovery phase that could persist for another six to nine months. Rather than expecting a rapid re-test of all-time highs, he said the more likely path is gradual improvement over time. For context on why Cole's perspective carries weight, Strive is a publicly traded firm that holds Bitcoin on its balance sheet. The company reported owning 43,000 BTC as of Oct. 23, per the figures referenced in the report. Several participants in the coverage emphasized the same distinction: the Binance breach did not equal a compromise of Bitcoin's core network. Wirex 's financial crime director Paul Chapman drew a sharp line between attacks on a company's internal systems and an actual hack of the cryptocurrency protocol. “It's important to be clear that Bitcoin itself hasn't been hacked - this was an attack on one company's systems, not the network,” Chapman told Cointelegraph. That distinction matters for investors because it separates two types of risk: platform-level operational and custody vulnerabilities on one hand, and systemic risks to the blockchain on the other. Even when the market reacts strongly to exchange incidents, analysts and executives typically treat these events as reminders to reassess counterparty safety, wallet management, and signing processes-rather than as evidence that Bitcoin's consensus is broken. According to Glassnode, Thursday's Binance breach was the largest cryptocurrency hack on record, with around $6.3 billion affected-more than the combined losses from the next nine largest crypto hacks. Glassnode also noted that three of the 10 largest crypto hacks occurred since the beginning of 2025, and each involved exchanges. The earlier record referenced in the reporting was the $1.5 billion Bybit exploit in February 2025. The comparison is instructive because it shows how exchange-driven disruptions have repeatedly shaped short-term price action without necessarily changing long-term network assumptions. After the Bybit hack, Bitcoin fell about 5% from nearly $100,000 to around $95,000 during the period of breach-related volatility, according to a Bitfinex market report. Additional context comes from data Anchorage Digital cited by CNBC, which put Bitcoin's average decline in the first 24 hours after previous crypto exchange exploits at 8.3%. In that light, the post-Binance drawdown observed in the immediate trading window-around 4% from before the incident began at the time the Saturday reading was recorded-appears comparatively milder, though traders will still be watching whether broader risk conditions worsen or stabilize. While the market focus is often on headlines and price swings, technical reporting in the coverage underscored that the nature of the breach is crucial for understanding where defenses failed. Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan said the attackers appeared to have compromised Binance's transaction signing process. Binance, according to the coverage, said it had found no evidence of leaked wallet private keys, though its investigation was ongoing. Ben-Natan's analysis, as reported, described an Ethereum transaction that contained 50 signed authorizations tied to different transaction counts. A matching authorization reportedly enabled attacker-controlled code to execute through the wallet. Ben-Natan argued that checks before signing could have prevented the malicious authorization from being approved. Whether or not Binance's implementation details ultimately align with that interpretation, the takeaway for builders and users is clear: even without leaked private keys, systems that authorize transactions through software signing flows can still be attacked if safeguards are insufficient. For the months ahead, the key thing market participants will watch is whether Bitcoin's stabilization after the Binance incident proves durable-Cole suggested a gradual recovery window-alongside whether exchanges accelerate improvements in signing, authorization controls, and incident transparency. Until investigators close remaining gaps, the biggest uncertainty is less about Bitcoin's network integrity and more about how quickly the broader industry can reduce the likelihood of similar failures. passages: A security incident at digital asset exchange Binance on Thursday affected some $6.3 billion in client assets, making it the largest crypto theft on record.
Experts whom CNBC interviewed said the security incidents on the crypto exchanges aren't surprising, especially in light of recent artificial intelligence hacking incidents .
That's because the hack may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, Binance said in a post on X .
Two high-profile security breaches this week – including the biggest cryptocurrency theft in history – are raising questions on the safety of storing funds in a wallet on a crypto exchange .
Binance and Polymarket reassured users that they would make affected investors whole.
That's a sign that users should feel confident in crypto exchanges, according to Ido Ben-Natan , CEO of blockchain security company Blockaid.

extraction.body: Two high-profile security breaches this week – including the biggest cryptocurrency theft in history – are raising questions on the safety of storing funds in a wallet on a crypto exchange . A security incident at digital asset exchange Binance on Thursday affected some $6.3 billion in client assets, making it the largest crypto theft on record. Earlier that day, prediction market platform Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international exchange after a third-party data provider was hacked, resulting in at least $2.7 million being drained from users' wallets. The company's international platform operates on the Polygon blockchain. Experts whom CNBC interviewed said the security incidents on the crypto exchanges aren't surprising, especially in light of recent artificial intelligence hacking incidents . Most of these experts even said that observers should expect more security incidents, at least in the near term, as that problem worsens. "I think it's extremely dangerous," said Tyler Moore, a cybersecurity professor at the University of Tulsa who has followed the asset class for more than a decade. "I think you should be very wary of leaving any significant amount of funds in an exchange… there are no built-in protections for when these inevitable hacks take place." For instance, banking customers can rely on the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation to insure deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, in the event of an institution's failure. There is no similar form of coverage available for funds lost from a cryptocurrency exchange, noted Moore. Binance and Polymarket reassured users that they would make affected investors whole. That's a sign that users should feel confident in crypto exchanges, according to Ido Ben-Natan , CEO of blockchain security company Blockaid. "I actually think no users will lose any money," he said. "Binance has said they're going to cover everything… I actually don't think it's a bad idea for users to put money in these exchanges. These exchanges need to work really hard to make sure they don't take another hit like this." Ben-Natan noted that while he thinks more hacks are likely as the cybersecurity landscape changes due to AI, he said it will only make the crypto industry stronger. As a result, a crypto wallet could ultimately become a safer place to hold funds compared to other options, since the industry will have the experience of how to handle these attacks, Ben-Natan said. A key point is that while Binance experienced a security incident on its offshore platform, its regulated, centralized U.S. exchange did not have a similar issue. The same was true of Polymarket's domestic exchange. U.S. regulated platforms Coinbase and Robinhood were also unaffected by the security breach on Binance, though shares of both fell on Friday in the aftermath. In a Friday appearance on CNBC's " Squawk on the Street ," the Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator of derivatives — Chairman Michael Selig said that the offshore nature of these incidents was critical to note. "They don't have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets," he said. "We want to offer a federal option to these exchanges to come and register with the CFTC, and they would be subject to the same sorts of cybersecurity safeguards that we have in our markets today." Brett Falk, a professor and director of the Crypto and Society Lab at the University of Pennsylvania, said that U.S. regulations likely wouldn't have stopped an incident like that of Binance on Thursday. That's because the hack may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, Binance said in a post on X . "Most of the regulation doesn't touch the specific software stack you have to use to authenticate people," Falk said. In another social media post, BInance later said its investigation uncovered additional points of breach , though the company didn't specify what they were. Falk echoed the argument by Ben-Natan that individuals likely won't face losses, and that it's better for traders to leave funds with an exchange where they have the financial backing of a company rather than in a self-custody wallet where no one can refund their losses in the event of a hack. Ben-Natan added that traders should feel secure based on how many incidents companies like his catch that don't become news. That's because the security technology often works and stops them before they become major incidents. However, crypto may be a unique target for hackers in a changing cybersecurity landscape, these experts told CNBC. That's because of how much liquidity individuals can quickly access in the event of a successful breach. It's why Ryan Kirkley, CEO of blockchain infrastructure company Global Settlement Network, thinks traders should be cautious leaving their funds in any wallet that's not backed by insurance until financial companies upgrade their security infrastructure. "I do not think there's anything right now that is a common solution in the marketplace where your assets are truly safe," Kirkley said. "Unless you are dealing with a reputable and firm broker-dealer that provides an asset insurance, you are risking your assets putting them into any ecosystem today just simply because there's so much unknown," he added. sources.title: Binance's $6.3 billion hack: How crypto insurance works
passages: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the world's biggest crypto heist, highlighting how cryptocurrency exchanges insure their digital assets against theft and cyberattacks.However, insurance protection varies widely.

Binance established the Secure Asset Fund for Users in July 2018 as an emergency reserve to protect users in extreme cases, such as security breaches or platform-level incidents.As of 2026, the SAFU fund holds crypto assets worth roughly $1 billion, entirely in bitcoin, according to Binance's website.

While cyber policies can cover both first-party losses and third-party liabilities, including forensic investigations, customer notifications and legal expenses, they generally exclude the loss or transfer of funds.As a result, standalone cyber policies typically do not cover the full value of stolen cryptocurrency unless specific digital asset coverage has been added.How do insurers assess crypto theft claims?Insurers examine how a breach occurred, which systems were compromised and whether the resulting loss falls within the policy's coverage.They may also assess whether the exchange followed the required security procedures, including controls over private keys, wallet access and transaction approvals.The distinction between an external hacker stealing credentials and an employee deliberately transferring assets can determine whether a crime or cyber insurance policy covers the loss.

sources.title: Binance’s $6.3 billion hack: What we know and what comes next - CNBC Africa
passages: Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets.
Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far.

Assuming frozen stablecoins are eventually returned, Binance’s SAFU emergency fund, worth approximately $1.2 billion, could cover roughly a third of the remaining losses, with the balance coming from the exchange’s own funds.

Chainalysis also pointed to North Korea, with co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin saying the firm assessed that the $6.4 billion Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, citing links to previous attacks.
The firm estimated that approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets were moved from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, with most transferred within about 20 minutes.
The FBI previously identified the same group as responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, according to the company’s insights.
“The most important takeaway for markets is that this does not currently appear to create meaningful solvency risk for Binance,” Farrell said.
TRM Labs said the Binance attack shared characteristics with previous North Korea-linked incidents, including preparations made well before the theft and transaction signatures obtained in advance.
Farrell said the key indicators to watch were how quickly Binance resumes withdrawals and whether outflows remain orderly.
He added that a shortfall in customer assets could force the exchange to sell reserves, potentially triggering broader selling across crypto markets.
The Binance hack underscores the need for stronger cybersecurity standards and greater coordination among governments, according to Chris Perkins, head of Franklin Crypto at Franklin Templeton.

extraction.body: Reach Africa's business leaders, investors and decision-makers. Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets. Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far. The exchange pledged to cover all losses, while blockchain investigators linked the attack to North Korea and analysts assessed the potential financial risks. Bitcoin was under pressure on Friday and was trading below $78,000. Freezing cryptocurrency prevents it from being transferred, but recovering the funds requires a separate legal process, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs and a former U.S. federal prosecutor and Treasury official. “A freeze stops the money from moving, and recovery follows through legal process,” Redbord told CNBC. Redbord said law enforcement typically obtains a court order or seizure warrant before working with stablecoin issuers to release or reissue assets and return them to their rightful owners. “Stablecoins are the most recoverable asset class in crypto because the issuer controls the token contract,” he said. “Tether and Circle can freeze, burn and reissue, which allows frozen USDT and USDC to be returned to a victim.” But recovering bitcoin and ether is more challenging because they have no issuer that can directly freeze the assets. Instead, investigators must trace funds through exchanges and other crypto services where they can potentially be intercepted, added Redbord. Eric Jardine, head of research at blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, said returning frozen assets requires coordination among law enforcement, exchanges and token issuers. “There is no standard recovery timeline. A technical freeze may happen quickly, while returning funds can take months or years,” Jardine told CNBC. Jardine added that while bitcoin and ether cannot be frozen by an issuer, they can still be traced and potentially recovered. Investigators can trace the funds on public blockchains and intervene when they reach a cooperating exchange or another centralized platform, he said. TRM Labs attributed the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit, based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The FBI previously identified the same group as responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, according to the company’s insights. TRM Labs said the Binance attack shared characteristics with previous North Korea-linked incidents, including preparations made well before the theft and transaction signatures obtained in advance. The firm estimated that approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets were moved from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, with most transferred within about 20 minutes. TRM Labs said preparations for the attack began at least 36 hours before the theft, with the attackers using Tornado Cash, a cryptocurrency mixing service, to fund their wallets ahead of the breach. Chainalysis also pointed to North Korea, with co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin saying the firm assessed that the $6.4 billion Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, citing links to previous attacks. The attack does not currently appear to pose a significant solvency risk for Binance, according to Sean Farrell, head of digital asset strategy at Fundstrat Global Advisors. “The most important takeaway for markets is that this does not currently appear to create meaningful solvency risk for Binance,” Farrell said. Farrell estimated that around $3.3 billion in assets remained unfrozen. Assuming frozen stablecoins are eventually returned, Binance’s SAFU emergency fund, worth approximately $1.2 billion, could cover roughly a third of the remaining losses, with the balance coming from the exchange’s own funds. Farrell said the key indicators to watch were how quickly Binance resumes withdrawals and whether outflows remain orderly. He added that a shortfall in customer assets could force the exchange to sell reserves, potentially triggering broader selling across crypto markets. “I do not think that is the setup we are dealing with, but the key tell will be how quickly withdrawals resume and whether outflows stay orderly,” Farrell said. The Binance hack underscores the need for stronger cybersecurity standards and greater coordination among governments, according to Chris Perkins, head of Franklin Crypto at Franklin Templeton. Speaking to CNBC’s “Squawk Box Asia,” Perkins said the industry must address cybersecurity challenges to reach its full potential, calling for stronger defenses and policies to hold cybercriminals accountable. “We need to make sure standards are incredibly high, but we have to really focus on the criminals,” Perkins said. Perkins called for greater international cooperation to address cybersecurity threats, pointing to regulatory coordination among G20 countries following the global financial crisis as a potential model. He also said AI could help improve cybersecurity by identifying and addressing vulnerabilities, even as the technology is used by both attackers and defenders. coreStoryFacts.text: A security incident at digital asset exchange Binance on Thursday affected some $6.3 billion in client assets, making it the largest crypto theft on record.
Experts whom CNBC interviewed said the security incidents on the crypto exchanges aren't surprising, especially in light of recent artificial intelligence hacking incidents .
That's because the hack may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, Binance said in a post on X .
Two high-profile security breaches this week – including the biggest cryptocurrency theft in history – are raising questions on the safety of storing funds in a wallet on a crypto exchange .
Binance and Polymarket reassured users that they would make affected investors whole.
That's a sign that users should feel confident in crypto exchanges, according to Ido Ben-Natan , CEO of blockchain security company Blockaid.
"I actually think no users will lose any money," he said.
"Binance has said they're going to cover everything… I actually don't think it's a bad idea for users to put money in these exchanges.
As a result, a crypto wallet could ultimately become a safer place to hold funds compared to other options, since the industry will have the experience of how to handle these attacks, Ben-Natan said.
However, crypto may be a unique target for hackers in a changing cybersecurity landscape, these experts told CNBC.

Earlier that day, prediction market platform Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international exchange after a third-party data provider was hacked, resulting in at least $2.7 million being drained from users' wallets.
The same was true of Polymarket's domestic exchange.
U.S. regulated platforms Coinbase and Robinhood were also unaffected by the security breach on Binance, though shares of both fell on Friday in the aftermath.
In another social media post, BInance later said its investigation uncovered additional points of breach , though the company didn't specify what they were.

Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the world's biggest crypto heist, highlighting how cryptocurrency exchanges insure their digital assets against theft and cyberattacks.However, insurance protection varies widely.

Binance established the Secure Asset Fund for Users in July 2018 as an emergency reserve to protect users in extreme cases, such as security breaches or platform-level incidents.As of 2026, the SAFU fund holds crypto assets worth roughly $1 billion, entirely in bitcoin, according to Binance's website.

extraction.body: Two high-profile security breaches this week – including the biggest cryptocurrency theft in history – are raising questions on the safety of storing funds in a wallet on a crypto exchange . A security incident at digital asset exchange Binance on Thursday affected some $6.3 billion in client assets, making it the largest crypto theft on record. Earlier that day, prediction market platform Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international exchange after a third-party data provider was hacked, resulting in at least $2.7 million being drained from users' wallets. The company's international platform operates on the Polygon blockchain. Experts whom CNBC interviewed said the security incidents on the crypto exchanges aren't surprising, especially in light of recent artificial intelligence hacking incidents . Most of these experts even said that observers should expect more security incidents, at least in the near term, as that problem worsens. "I think it's extremely dangerous," said Tyler Moore, a cybersecurity professor at the University of Tulsa who has followed the asset class for more than a decade. "I think you should be very wary of leaving any significant amount of funds in an exchange… there are no built-in protections for when these inevitable hacks take place." For instance, banking customers can rely on the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation to insure deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, in the event of an institution's failure. There is no similar form of coverage available for funds lost from a cryptocurrency exchange, noted Moore. Binance and Polymarket reassured users that they would make affected investors whole. That's a sign that users should feel confident in crypto exchanges, according to Ido Ben-Natan , CEO of blockchain security company Blockaid. "I actually think no users will lose any money," he said. "Binance has said they're going to cover everything… I actually don't think it's a bad idea for users to put money in these exchanges. These exchanges need to work really hard to make sure they don't take another hit like this." Ben-Natan noted that while he thinks more hacks are likely as the cybersecurity landscape changes due to AI, he said it will only make the crypto industry stronger. As a result, a crypto wallet could ultimately become a safer place to hold funds compared to other options, since the industry will have the experience of how to handle these attacks, Ben-Natan said. A key point is that while Binance experienced a security incident on its offshore platform, its regulated, centralized U.S. exchange did not have a similar issue. The same was true of Polymarket's domestic exchange. U.S. regulated platforms Coinbase and Robinhood were also unaffected by the security breach on Binance, though shares of both fell on Friday in the aftermath. In a Friday appearance on CNBC's " Squawk on the Street ," the Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator of derivatives — Chairman Michael Selig said that the offshore nature of these incidents was critical to note. "They don't have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets," he said. "We want to offer a federal option to these exchanges to come and register with the CFTC, and they would be subject to the same sorts of cybersecurity safeguards that we have in our markets today." Brett Falk, a professor and director of the Crypto and Society Lab at the University of Pennsylvania, said that U.S. regulations likely wouldn't have stopped an incident like that of Binance on Thursday. That's because the hack may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, Binance said in a post on X . "Most of the regulation doesn't touch the specific software stack you have to use to authenticate people," Falk said. In another social media post, BInance later said its investigation uncovered additional points of breach , though the company didn't specify what they were. Falk echoed the argument by Ben-Natan that individuals likely won't face losses, and that it's better for traders to leave funds with an exchange where they have the financial backing of a company rather than in a self-custody wallet where no one can refund their losses in the event of a hack. Ben-Natan added that traders should feel secure based on how many incidents companies like his catch that don't become news. That's because the security technology often works and stops them before they become major incidents. However, crypto may be a unique target for hackers in a changing cybersecurity landscape, these experts told CNBC. That's because of how much liquidity individuals can quickly access in the event of a successful breach. It's why Ryan Kirkley, CEO of blockchain infrastructure company Global Settlement Network, thinks traders should be cautious leaving their funds in any wallet that's not backed by insurance until financial companies upgrade their security infrastructure. "I do not think there's anything right now that is a common solution in the marketplace where your assets are truly safe," Kirkley said. "Unless you are dealing with a reputable and firm broker-dealer that provides an asset insurance, you are risking your assets putting them into any ecosystem today just simply because there's so much unknown," he added. Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets. Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far. The exchange pledged to cover all losses, while blockchain investigators linked the attack to North Korea and analysts assessed the potential financial risks. extraction.body: The $6.3 billion theft from Binance raises alarms over future cyber threats, experts warn. NEW DELHI, Oct 31: Hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets from Binance, one of the largest thefts in financial history. Founder Changpeng Zhao acknowledged the breach and thanked other cryptocurrency companies for assisting in freezing affected assets. Eric Schiffer, chairman of Patriarch and Reputation Management Consultants, warned this incident could signal a surge in cyberattacks as artificial intelligence advances. He said, “I think the bloodbath of AI hacking is to come. And there’s going to be a lot more pain.” Schiffer stressed that cybersecurity must be prioritized proactively. In response to the hack, Binance set aside over $6.34 billion of its own funds to cover losses, with $5 billion already in the stolen cryptocurrencies. The company temporarily suspended withdrawals during security checks. About $3 billion of the stolen assets have been frozen with help from industry partners. Binance stated it would absorb the financial impact of the breach, assuring customers they would not bear the losses. This incident raised concerns about investor confidence, but Schiffer believes Binance will recover due to its strong balance sheet. The investigation revealed a compromised laptop as the initial entry point, with additional vulnerabilities discovered later. Binance confirmed that its internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets were accessed, allowing unauthorized withdrawals of significant amounts. Former President Donald Trump noted that his administration is investigating the possibility of North Korean hackers being behind the breach. He expressed concerns about the risks of cryptocurrency, stating, “I’ve always felt it was a little bit dangerous.” The U.S. Secret Service is collaborating with private-sector partners to trace and recover the stolen funds. Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs suggested the attack was executed by TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit, based on high confidence in their intelligence data. For investors, Schiffer recommended evaluating the reliability of cryptocurrency trading platforms and urged caution in choosing where to store digital assets, questioning if they trust the brands involved. Deputies were called to The Cut Bar and Restaurant at 2570 Business Park Court just after 1:45 a.m. to investigate a report of a shooting and stabbing. The sheriff’s office said a private security guard attempted to intervene in a fight between two men when one of them, William Pierre Strong, 41, of Waldorf, threatened the other man with a knife. The security guard tried to take the knife but Strong stabbed the victim in the abdomen, investigators said. The sheriff’s office said that Strong then “appeared to make another attempt to stab the victim.” It was then that the security guard shot Strong, hitting him once in the chest, the sheriff’s office said in a release. The wounded Strong walked out of the bar and collapsed in the parking lot, the sheriff’s office said, and arriving deputies “located him with the knife still in his hand.” The man who was stabbed in the incident suffered injuries that “do not appear to be life-threatening,” according to the sheriff’s office. The case will be presented to the state’s attorney’s office for review, according to a news release. Anyone with information regarding this case is asked to call the Charles County Sheriff’s Office at 301-609-6436. extraction.body: WALDORF, MD — A 41-year-old Waldorf man was fatally shot by a private security guard after stabbing another man during an altercation inside a Waldorf bar early Saturday morning, according to the Charles County Sheriff's Office. William Pierre Strong, 41, died after being shot once in the chest at The Cut Bar & Restaurant, located at 2570 Business Park Court, authorities said. Deputies responded to the establishment around 1:46 a.m. for reports of a stabbing and shooting. According to the preliminary investigation, two men reportedly got into an altercation inside the bar. Police said Strong pulled out a knife and threatened the other man. A private security guard assigned to the business attempted to intervene and gain control of Strong's hand and the knife, authorities said. During the confrontation, Strong stabbed the other man once in the abdomen. As Strong appeared to attempt another stabbing, the security guard fired his gun, striking Strong once in the chest, according to investigators. Strong walked outside the establishment before collapsing in the parking lot. Responding deputies found him with the knife still in his hand. Deputies and emergency medical personnel attempted to save his life, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. The man who suffered the stab wound was treated for injuries that did not appear to be life-threatening. extraction.body: Stablecoin issuers froze about $2.4 billion of the roughly $6.4 billion stolen. The rest exceeds Binance’s insurance fund, and the man promising to make users whole isn’t supposed to be running the company. A notorious North Korean cybercrime group has stolen around $6.4 billion in cryptoassets from multiple hot wallets a belonging to Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, and still controls around $3 billion of it after stablecoin issuers and other protocols froze what they could. These estimates are still in flux as various platforms work to freeze tokens or otherwise thwart the attacker from cashing out, and as both Binance and independent security researchers continue their investigations. Unlike many supposedly “multi-billion dollar” crypto hacks, where the headline figure relies on the notional value of illiquid assets that could never be sold for anywhere near that amount, the majority of these stolen assets were major stablecoins, bitcoin, ethereum, and other fairly liquid tokens. Binance has estimated the total theft at $6.3 billion; external estimates later revised the total up to around $6.4 billion. At least $5.5 billion of these were liquid assets. Tether announced they had frozen at least $1.567 billion of the stolen USDT, and Circle has frozen around $800 million of stolen USDC. World Liberty Financial froze the $27 million in USD1 stolen by the attacker, and the Arbitrum ethereum layer-2 network froze an additional $30.5 million that had moved to its network. The attacker is estimated to have made off with between $2.4 billion and $3.4 billion . Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, who is legally not allowed to have any active role with the company [ I98 ] yet still has remarkable amounts of inside knowledge into its inner workings, posted on Twitter less than an hour after the theft that “User funds are safe!”, adding early estimates of how much Tether and Circle had frozen. He added, “I don't manage Binance (.com) anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” He later tweeted “Loss might be a bit higher than [$1 billion], but will cover.” (Why a person who is barred from any control over Binance would be the one promising this is an exercise I will leave to the reader.) Binance keeps an emergency insurance fund in case of exploits or other crypto disasters. Its most recent balance report puts it at around $1.3 billion. 1 Unless more is recovered, Binance will either fail to make users whole or dip into its own balance sheet — potentially to the tune of 10 figures. Binance later wrote that their "initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop", which allowed an attacker to “submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” They estimated the total theft at around $6.3 billion, with approximately $3 billion frozen. 2 While the assets frozen by Tether and Circle will likely easily be returned to Binance, other non-centralized assets frozen by various protocols may be inaccessible both to the attacker and to Binance. Blockchain security firm TRM Labs has attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group. 3 The group has been linked to other massive cryptocurrency heists, including a massive $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit cryptocurrency exchange in 2025 [ W3IGG ]. This Binance hack has now surpassed the Bybit hack for the largest cryptocurrency theft. I’ve written more about North Korea’s crypto thefts, how they launder the funds, and what the money pays for in a follow-up. The contagion also threatens to spread beyond Binance. Aave, a defi lending project, paused some of its markets to stop the attacker from depositing stolen assets as collateral and borrowing against them — a move that could otherwise leave it holding significant bad debt. Protocols that are slower to respond may not be so lucky. The Binance theft came within hours of a separate, much smaller theft of around $2.7 million from Polymarket users [ W3IGG ], and some people wondered whether the two were connected. I doubt it. Polymarket has blamed its incident on a compromised third-party vendor, which an attacker apparently used to inject a malicious script into the site’s frontend and steal user funds. The Binance attacker got access to the exchange’s own hot wallets. They’re very different attacks, and nothing besides timing ties them together so far. October 29 at 8:47pm: Updated to remove some skepticism around whether bitcoin attributed to the attacker was stolen, after a conversation with another researcher made me less confident the wallets were unrelated. October 30 at 1:17am: Updated with a statement from Binance and the report from TRM Labs. October 30 at 1:05pm: Updated with a link to my primer on North Korean crypto thefts , and with a revised total theft estimate from outside blockchain analytics firms. Exchanges hold most customer funds in “cold” wallets, more secure crypto wallets whose keys are kept offline and where assets are hard to move quickly. Cybercriminals swiped the digital coins out of Binance wallets within a mere 20 minutes starting at 4:30 p.m. ET Thursday, exploiting the system by hacking into an engineer’s laptop, according to analytics firm TRM Labs and industry insiders.

Binance initially said the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop. In an update Friday, Richard Teng, co-CEO of Binance, said the company’s security team has “uncovered additional points of breach,” suggesting it was a complex attack carried out by more than one person.

US officials have said cybercrime attacks fund roughly half of North Korea’s missile program.

Bitcoin dropped below $80,000 for the first time in a month, ether fell to a two-month low of $2,230 and crypto-related stocks plummeted as the hack served as a stunning reminder that the crypto industry still remains a largely unregulated Wild West.

extraction.body: A security guard shot and killed a man suspected of stabbing another man at a bar early Saturday morning in Waldorf, Maryland, the Charles County sheriff’s office said. Deputies were called to The Cut Bar and Restaurant at 2570 Business Park Court just after 1:45 a.m. to investigate a report of a shooting and stabbing. The sheriff’s office said a private security guard attempted to intervene in a fight between two men when one of them, William Pierre Strong, 41, of Waldorf, threatened the other man with a knife. The security guard tried to take the knife but Strong stabbed the victim in the abdomen, investigators said. The sheriff’s office said that Strong then “appeared to make another attempt to stab the victim.” It was then that the security guard shot Strong, hitting him once in the chest, the sheriff’s office said in a release. The wounded Strong walked out of the bar and collapsed in the parking lot, the sheriff’s office said, and arriving deputies “located him with the knife still in his hand.” The man who was stabbed in the incident suffered injuries that “do not appear to be life-threatening,” according to the sheriff’s office. The case will be presented to the state’s attorney’s office for review, according to a news release. Anyone with information regarding this case is asked to call the Charles County Sheriff’s Office at 301-609-6436. extraction.body: A private security guard fatally shot a 41-year-old Waldorf man early Saturday after the man stabbed someone else during a fight inside a bar on Business Park Court, according to investigators. William Pierre Strong was pronounced dead at the scene, while the man he stabbed was treated for injuries that did not appear to be life-threatening. Charles County deputies responded to The Cut Bar & Restaurant at 2570 Business Park Court in Waldorf around 1:46 a.m. Saturday for a report of a stabbing and shooting, according to FOX 5 DC . Investigators said a confrontation between two men escalated when one of them pulled out a knife and threatened the other, the station reported. A security guard working at the bar then stepped in, trying to take control of the man's hand and the knife, according to WJLA . Despite the intervention, the man stabbed the other man once in the abdomen, the outlet reported. Investigators said the guard fired his gun as Strong appeared to attempt another stabbing, striking him once in the chest. WJLA reported that Strong then walked outside and collapsed in the parking lot. Responding officers found him still holding the knife, per the same account. Officers and emergency medical personnel provided aid, but Strong was pronounced dead at the scene. The man who was stabbed was treated for injuries that did not appear to be life-threatening. Authorities have not released the identities of the stabbing victim or the security guard, according to FOX 5 DC. The WBFF report on the incident noted that no charges had been announced in the sheriff's office release. Detectives are investigating Strong's death as a homicide and plan to present the case to the Charles County State's Attorney's Office for review, authorities said. The sheriff's office has asked the public for any information related to the incident, and those with details can reach Detective Logsdon at 301-609-6436. extraction.body: A security guard shot and killed a man suspected of stabbing another man at a bar early Saturday morning in Waldorf, Maryland, the Charles County sheriff’s office said. Deputies were called to The Cut Bar and Restaurant at 2570 Business Park Court just after 1:45 a.m. to investigate a report of a shooting and stabbing. The sheriff’s office said a private security guard attempted to intervene in a fight between two men when one of them, William Pierre Strong, 41, of Waldorf, threatened the other man with a knife. The security guard tried to take the knife but Strong stabbed the victim in the abdomen, investigators said. The sheriff’s office said that Strong then “appeared to make another attempt to stab the victim.” It was then that the security guard shot Strong, hitting him once in the chest, the sheriff’s office said in a release. The wounded Strong walked out of the bar and collapsed in the parking lot, the sheriff’s office said, and arriving deputies “located him with the knife still in his hand.” The man who was stabbed in the incident suffered injuries that “do not appear to be life-threatening,” according to the sheriff’s office. The case will be presented to the state’s attorney’s office for review, according to a news release. Anyone with information regarding this case is asked to call the Charles County Sheriff’s Office at 301-609-6436. extraction.body: A private security guard fatally shot a 41-year-old Waldorf man early Saturday after the man stabbed someone else during a fight inside a bar on Business Park Court, according to investigators. William Pierre Strong was pronounced dead at the scene, while the man he stabbed was treated for injuries that did not appear to be life-threatening. Charles County deputies responded to The Cut Bar & Restaurant at 2570 Business Park Court in Waldorf around 1:46 a.m. Saturday for a report of a stabbing and shooting, according to FOX 5 DC . Investigators said a confrontation between two men escalated when one of them pulled out a knife and threatened the other, the station reported. A security guard working at the bar then stepped in, trying to take control of the man's hand and the knife, according to WJLA . Despite the intervention, the man stabbed the other man once in the abdomen, the outlet reported. Investigators said the guard fired his gun as Strong appeared to attempt another stabbing, striking him once in the chest. WJLA reported that Strong then walked outside and collapsed in the parking lot. Responding officers found him still holding the knife, per the same account. Officers and emergency medical personnel provided aid, but Strong was pronounced dead at the scene. The man who was stabbed was treated for injuries that did not appear to be life-threatening. Authorities have not released the identities of the stabbing victim or the security guard, according to FOX 5 DC. The WBFF report on the incident noted that no charges had been announced in the sheriff's office release. Detectives are investigating Strong's death as a homicide and plan to present the case to the Charles County State's Attorney's Office for review, authorities said. The sheriff's office has asked the public for any information related to the incident, and those with details can reach Detective Logsdon at 301-609-6436. The shooting echoes a similar case in Baltimore County, where an armed security guard shot and killed a knife-wielding man inside Crackpot Bar in Towson during an early-morning confrontation, according to CBS Baltimore . “We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles,” an Amazon spokesperson said, without providing further details.Also Read | Amazon layoffs hit India again as company cuts 1,000 jobs globally: ReportThe cuts affected no more than 250 employees, primarily in software development, according to a person familiar with the matter.

“We've adjusted parts of our Stores business because we believe this structure will better enable us to deliver on our priorities”, the spokesperson said. the company refused to reveal how many employees in India were impacted by the layoffs.In January, the company had announced 16,000 global job cuts amid ‘rising competition over AI’.In October 2025, amazon cut around 14,000 jobs.

CEO Jassy had reportedly said that Amazon’s rapid growth in its workforce, operations and business segments in recent years had led to an increase in staffing and management layers.

extraction.body: New Delhi: Amazon has laid off around 250 employees from its devices and services division, with software development roles bearing the brunt of the latest job cuts. The move comes as the company expands its artificial intelligence (AI) investments and makes AI a central part of its engineering operations. The layoffs were announced on Wednesday, the same day Amazon introduced five new devices with Alexa, like a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart screen, an Alexa Photo Frame, and the Echo Time bedside clock. The devices division makes products like Kindle e-readers and Echo smart speakers. Amazon confirmed the job cuts after a Reuters inquiry but did not disclose the number of employees affected. A person familiar with the matter said the reductions involved no more than 250 positions. "We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles," an Amazon spokesperson said, adding that the changes would help the company “operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadmap.” Employees Informed Through Early Morning Emails Affected employees were informed about the layoffs through emails and text messages sent early Wednesday morning, according to Reuters. One email cited in the report was sent by Cherie Robinson, a vice president in Amazon's devices and services division. Robinson wrote that the company had conducted "a thorough review of our structure," which led to the decision to cut jobs. Early morning notifications have also featured in previous rounds of job cuts at other technology companies, including Meta and Oracle. The latest reductions come shortly after Amazon published a September memo from its engineering leadership outlining how developers should adapt to the growing use of AI in software development. "We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind," the memo said, underlining the company's push to make AI a key part of its engineering practices. Fresh Cuts Follow Thousands Of Job Losses The layoffs in the devices division follow Amazon's decision earlier this month to eliminate around 1,000 jobs in its core retail business. The company had also announced 16,000 job cuts in January, following the elimination of 14,000 positions in October last year. Amazon is simultaneously committing substantial resources to AI, with its investment in the technology expected to reach as much as $220 billion this year. The latest layoffs are happening just before the company shares its third-quarter earnings results, which are set to be announced after the markets close on Thursday. Amazon is not alone in reducing its workforce as technology companies reassess their operations and spending priorities. According to reports, more than 135,000 technology jobs have been eliminated this year. Dropbox recently announced plans to cut 9 per cent of its global workforce, while Microsoft has offered voluntary exit options to roughly 60,000 employees, or around one-fourth of its total workforce.

“We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles,” an Amazon spokesperson said, without providing further details.Also Read | Amazon layoffs hit India again as company cuts 1,000 jobs globally: ReportThe cuts affected no more than 250 employees, primarily in software development, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Layoffs expected to help streamline operations: SpokespersonAccording to the spokesperson, the layoffs are intended to help Amazon “operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadmap”.As is customary at Amazon, workers were notified of the cuts through text messages and emails sent early Wednesday morning.
CEO Jassy had reportedly said that Amazon’s rapid growth in its workforce, operations and business segments in recent years had led to an increase in staffing and management layers.

US-based AI data services company Innodata fired 550 employees in India, reported the ‘The Economic Times.’ In a separate round of firing the tech and e-commerce company Amazon laid off around 250 employees from its Devices and Services unit.
According to a Reuters report, Amazon has confirmed the layoffs.
Message to engineers: Adopt AI or risk being left behind
Amazon has witnessed large-scale layoffs over the past year.
Earlier, in January this year, the company laid off 16,000 employees, while another 14,000 people were made redundant in October last year.
Just one day before the news of layoffs emerged, Amazon sent an internal message to its software engineers.
In the message, titled 'The Role of Developers in the Age of AI', the company's engineering leaders made it clear that it no longer matters which tool you use; what matters most is the result.
Notably, the decision to cut jobs in the devices division came on the same day that Amazon launched its five new Alexa-powered smart devices on the market.
The company is introducing its voice assistant in a new avatar amid stiff competition from rivals such as Apple and OpenAI.

"We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles," an Amazon spokesperson said, adding that the changes would help the company “operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadmap.” Employees Informed Through Early Morning Emails Affected employees were informed about the layoffs through emails and text messages sent early Wednesday morning, according to Reuters.
New Delhi: Amazon has laid off around 250 employees from its devices and services division, with software development roles bearing the brunt of the latest job cuts.
Early morning notifications have also featured in previous rounds of job cuts at other technology companies, including Meta and Oracle.
Amazon confirmed the job cuts after a Reuters inquiry but did not disclose the number of employees affected.

The layoffs were announced on Wednesday, the same day Amazon introduced five new devices with Alexa, like a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart screen, an Alexa Photo Frame, and the Echo Time bedside clock.
A person familiar with the matter said the reductions involved no more than 250 positions.
Amazon recently laid off more than 250 employees from its Devices and Services unit, most of whom were working in software development.

extraction.body: New Delhi: Amazon has laid off around 250 employees from its devices and services division, with software development roles bearing the brunt of the latest job cuts. The move comes as the company expands its artificial intelligence (AI) investments and makes AI a central part of its engineering operations. The layoffs were announced on Wednesday, the same day Amazon introduced five new devices with Alexa, like a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart screen, an Alexa Photo Frame, and the Echo Time bedside clock. The devices division makes products like Kindle e-readers and Echo smart speakers. Amazon confirmed the job cuts after a Reuters inquiry but did not disclose the number of employees affected. A person familiar with the matter said the reductions involved no more than 250 positions. "We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles," an Amazon spokesperson said, adding that the changes would help the company “operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadmap.” Employees Informed Through Early Morning Emails Affected employees were informed about the layoffs through emails and text messages sent early Wednesday morning, according to Reuters. One email cited in the report was sent by Cherie Robinson, a vice president in Amazon's devices and services division. Robinson wrote that the company had conducted "a thorough review of our structure," which led to the decision to cut jobs. Early morning notifications have also featured in previous rounds of job cuts at other technology companies, including Meta and Oracle. The latest reductions come shortly after Amazon published a September memo from its engineering leadership outlining how developers should adapt to the growing use of AI in software development. "We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind," the memo said, underlining the company's push to make AI a key part of its engineering practices. Fresh Cuts Follow Thousands Of Job Losses The layoffs in the devices division follow Amazon's decision earlier this month to eliminate around 1,000 jobs in its core retail business. The company had also announced 16,000 job cuts in January, following the elimination of 14,000 positions in October last year. Amazon is simultaneously committing substantial resources to AI, with its investment in the technology expected to reach as much as $220 billion this year. The latest layoffs are happening just before the company shares its third-quarter earnings results, which are set to be announced after the markets close on Thursday. Amazon is not alone in reducing its workforce as technology companies reassess their operations and spending priorities. According to reports, more than 135,000 technology jobs have been eliminated this year. Dropbox recently announced plans to cut 9 per cent of its global workforce, while Microsoft has offered voluntary exit options to roughly 60,000 employees, or around one-fourth of its total workforce.

sources.title: Shigeru Miyamoto Declares November 1st Pikmin Day In Surprise Nintendo Direct - Kotaku
passages: Shigeru Miyamoto can drop a new holiday altogether.
This morning, Nintendo announced a spur of the moment Nintendo Direct.

In it, Miyamoto declares that tomorrow, November 1st, will henceforth be known as ‘ Pikmin Day.’ While the Direct had updates for two of the most recent Olimar adventures, it did not provide information about any new games.

Miyamoto’s reasoning is that if three Pikmin stood shoulder to shoulder, they would resemble the date ‘11.1.’ Though this conflicts with the Day of the Dead, experienced players know there are probably some deceased Pikmin spirits you could atone to.
It doesn’t hurt that in two weeks, the Nintendo Switch 2 edition of Pikmin 4 will drop.
Nintendo Nintendo Direct Pikmin Pikmin 4 pikmin bloom
The direct ended on a new animated Pikmin short, adding that the once mysterious cartoons will soon be a monthly occurrence.
Miyamoto also introduced actress and Pikmin ambassador Fuka Koshiba, who caught his eye crocheting hats.
Happy Pikmin Day eve, everyone. I hope you are doing well.

While the surprise Direct didn’t provide any surprise new games, it did bring information on what the new edition will offer, plus an update on the mobile Pikmin Bloom . Hopefully more dependably than what Hey You, Pikachu! could pull off . The new version will also feature an exclusive new mode, ‘Dandori Academy,’ a timed treasure rush. Akin to the gauntlets of the console series, these caves promise heaps of treasure at the risk of total Pikmin devastation. sources.title: Nintendo Reveals Pikmin Day Surprise and New Project Hello! Pikmin - Polygon.com
passages: 1 was chosen as the annual Pikmin Day because the date's appearance (i.e., 11.1) resembles the original red, yellow, and blue Pikmin standing side by side.
Miyamoto also revealed a new Pikmin project called Hello!
Pikmin that he's collaborating on with Nintendo Pictures .
Let's back up, since you don't appear to be aware that today's Pikmin Day Eve.
Nintendo announced Saturday that, going forward, Nov.
1 will be known as Pikmin Day , a planned annual celebration of the now-25-year-old puzzle-strategy franchise.
Nintendo designer Shigeru Miyamoto announced the news alongside a handful of updates for games like Pikmin 4 and Pikmin Bloom during a brief video dedicated to the Pikmin franchise.
After the video, Miyamoto said Nintendo plans to release new animated shorts in the Hello!
Pikmin series through the Nintendo Today app and other channels.
Nintendo Pictures released a Pikmin-themed animated short titled "Close to You" one year ago to strong reception and interest.

Prior to that, Miyamoto and company released a series of Pikmin animations ("The Night Juicer," "Treasure in a Bottle," and "Occupational Hazards") back in 2014, reflecting what has long been a fascination for the game developer and creator of Pikmin.
As previously announced, Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will feature Switch 2-exclusive features and challenges.
Oatchi, the game's puppy-like companion, can now be called to action with voice commands using the Switch 2's built-in microphone.
Limited-time exams will be released every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, with leaderboards so players can compete to see who's got the best strats.
The humorous animation shows a red Pikmin approaching a seemingly sleeping toad as the pint-sized creature attempts to steal a well-worn baseball.

Beyond games, Miyamoto revealed he has recruited popular Japanese actor Fuka Koshiba as a spokesperson for the game franchise — specifically "to build more excitement about Pikmin going forward." Koshiba isn't just a successful and famous actor, she's also known to knit Pikmin-themed headwear in her spare time.
Nintendo's mobile Pikmin game, Pikmin Bloom , is getting a new feature this winter called Secret Caves.
The new feature will let players send their Pikmin hordes into caves to battle enemies and collect treasure.

It’s 10 p.m. — do you know where your Pikmin are?

Happy early Pikmin Day! Wait. Let's back up, since you don't appear to be aware that today's Pikmin Day Eve. Nintendo announced Saturday that, going forward, Nov. 1 will be known as Pikmin Day , a planned annual celebration of the now-25-year-old puzzle-strategy franchise. Nintendo designer Shigeru Miyamoto announced the news alongside a handful of updates for games like Pikmin 4 and Pikmin Bloom during a brief video dedicated to the Pikmin franchise.

In that video, Miyamoto explains that Nov. 1 was chosen as the annual Pikmin Day because the date's appearance (i.e., 11.1) resembles the original red, yellow, and blue Pikmin standing side by side. Miyamoto also revealed a new Pikmin project called Hello! Pikmin that he's collaborating on with Nintendo Pictures .

Miyamoto showed a new short animated feature that will be part of the Hello! Pikmin series. The humorous animation shows a red Pikmin approaching a seemingly sleeping toad as the pint-sized creature attempts to steal a well-worn baseball. As the video plays out, it seems the red Pikmin's fate is sealed; the toad isn't asleep after all. And it's hungry.

After the video, Miyamoto said Nintendo plans to release new animated shorts in the Hello! Pikmin series through the Nintendo Today app and other channels. He's collaborating with the Nintendo Pictures team to make them and they plan to release one video per month in the near future.

Nintendo Pictures released a Pikmin-themed animated short titled "Close to You" one year ago to strong reception and interest. Prior to that, Miyamoto and company released a series of Pikmin animations ("The Night Juicer," "Treasure in a Bottle," and "Occupational Hazards") back in 2014, reflecting what has long been a fascination for the game developer and creator of Pikmin.

The Nintendo Switch 2 Edition of Pikmin 4 arrives in November with the new Dandori Academy bonus content. During Saturday's Pikmin showcase, Miyamoto walked Switch 2 owners through what's coming and how the rerelease will stand apart from the original Nintendo Switch release of Pikmin 4 .

As previously announced, Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will feature Switch 2-exclusive features and challenges. Oatchi, the game's puppy-like companion, can now be called to action with voice commands using the Switch 2's built-in microphone. Dandori Academy mode adds new tests that will task Pikmin 4 players with optimizing their strategies. Limited-time exams will be released every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, with leaderboards so players can compete to see who's got the best strats. Seventy-two Dandori Academy stages will be released over time.
A free demo of Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will launch on Nov. 2, letting Switch 2 owners play the opening area and two Dandori Academy challenges.
It’s 10 p.m. — do you know where your Pikmin are?

Nintendo's mobile Pikmin game, Pikmin Bloom , is getting a new feature this winter called Secret Caves. The new feature will let players send their Pikmin hordes into caves to battle enemies and collect treasure. That booty will be part of a new in-game collection, giving Pikmin Bloom players new collectibles to hunt for.
Getting into Pikmin Bloom 's Secret Cave requires maps, which can be acquired through in-game postcards as well as by playing Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition 's Dandori Academy challenges.
Pikmin Bloom is available for free on Android and iOS devices.
Niantic’s walking companion app has become a daily habit

Beyond games, Miyamoto revealed he has recruited popular Japanese actor Fuka Koshiba as a spokesperson for the game franchise — specifically "to build more excitement about Pikmin going forward." Koshiba isn't just a successful and famous actor, she's also known to knit Pikmin-themed headwear in her spare time.

In that video, Miyamoto explains that Nov. 1 was chosen as the annual Pikmin Day because the date's appearance (i.e., 11.1) resembles the original red, yellow, and blue Pikmin standing side by side. Miyamoto also revealed a new Pikmin project called Hello! Pikmin that he's collaborating on with Nintendo Pictures .

Miyamoto showed a new short animated feature that will be part of the Hello! Pikmin series. The humorous animation shows a red Pikmin approaching a seemingly sleeping toad as the pint-sized creature attempts to steal a well-worn baseball. As the video plays out, it seems the red Pikmin's fate is sealed; the toad isn't asleep after all. And it's hungry.

After the video, Miyamoto said Nintendo plans to release new animated shorts in the Hello! Pikmin series through the Nintendo Today app and other channels. He's collaborating with the Nintendo Pictures team to make them and they plan to release one video per month in the near future.

Nintendo Pictures released a Pikmin-themed animated short titled "Close to You" one year ago to strong reception and interest. Prior to that, Miyamoto and company released a series of Pikmin animations ("The Night Juicer," "Treasure in a Bottle," and "Occupational Hazards") back in 2014, reflecting what has long been a fascination for the game developer and creator of Pikmin.

The Nintendo Switch 2 Edition of Pikmin 4 arrives in November with the new Dandori Academy bonus content. During Saturday's Pikmin showcase, Miyamoto walked Switch 2 owners through what's coming and how the rerelease will stand apart from the original Nintendo Switch release of Pikmin 4 .

As previously announced, Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will feature Switch 2-exclusive features and challenges. Oatchi, the game's puppy-like companion, can now be called to action with voice commands using the Switch 2's built-in microphone. Dandori Academy mode adds new tests that will task Pikmin 4 players with optimizing their strategies. Limited-time exams will be released every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, with leaderboards so players can compete to see who's got the best strats. Seventy-two Dandori Academy stages will be released over time.
A free demo of Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will launch on Nov. 2, letting Switch 2 owners play the opening area and two Dandori Academy challenges.
It’s 10 p.m. — do you know where your Pikmin are?

Nintendo's mobile Pikmin game, Pikmin Bloom , is getting a new feature this winter called Secret Caves. The new feature will let players send their Pikmin hordes into caves to battle enemies and collect treasure. That booty will be part of a new in-game collection, giving Pikmin Bloom players new collectibles to hunt for.
Getting into Pikmin Bloom 's Secret Cave requires maps, which can be acquired through in-game postcards as well as by playing Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition 's Dandori Academy challenges.
Pikmin Bloom is available for free on Android and iOS devices.
Niantic’s walking companion app has become a daily habit

Beyond games, Miyamoto revealed he has recruited popular Japanese actor Fuka Koshiba as a spokesperson for the game franchise — specifically "to build more excitement about Pikmin going forward." Koshiba isn't just a successful and famous actor, she's also known to knit Pikmin-themed headwear in her spare time.
A dark detective thriller where folklore is real, violence is chilling, and every choice has consequences.

The gift card will be automatically added to your cart when you preorder one of Apple’s highest-end laptops available in 14- or 16-inch configurations, and even one of its 14-inch MacBook Pro laptops with the M6 chip. Di Benedetto got a chance to check out the new laptop at Apple’s event, and came away impressed by the Tandem OLED panel’s brightness and contrast, but described the update as “kind of boring” given the relatively small changes to the system otherwise. There are some unique changes to macOS that help make the new touch experience smoother, like magnifying the traffic light-colored buttons on windows when you move your finger near them. The PROLED laptops are also a bit thinner and lighter than standard models, and the Apple logo on the back glows like on older versions. Read our MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display hands-on.

extraction.body: FREE $100 GIFT CARD: As of March 5, you can get a free $100 gift card when you pre-order the new Apple MacBook Pro with the M5 Pro or M5 Max chip at Best Buy. The premium laptops will begin shipping on March 11. Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple MacBook Pro (M5 Pro) Starting at $2,199 + free $100 gift card Preorder at Best Buy Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple MacBook Pro (M5 Max) Starting at $3,599 + free $100 gift card Preorder at Best Buy As you've likely seen by now, Apple had a big week. The company dropped a batch of new products, from the first-ever budget MacBook to an even more powerful MacBook Pro. The latter is pretty darn expensive, but if you lock in a preorder at Best Buy, you'll get a little relief in the form of a free gift card. As of March 5, when you pre-order the new MacBook Pro with either the M5 Pro or M5 Max chip at Best Buy (in any configuration), you'll get a free $100 e-gift card to spend however you please. The laptops will begin shipping on March 11 and you'll receive an email with your free gift once the laptop is in your possession. Sign Me Up By signing up, you agree to receive recurring automated SMS marketing messages from Mashable Deals at the number provided. The new M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros come in two sizes, 14 or 16 inches, and are essentially more powerful versions of the already stellar M5 MacBook Pro. The M5 Pro variants start at $2,199 for the 14-inch laptop and $2,699 for the 16-inch laptop and come with 1TB of base storage. They're built for folks "running complex workflows, like coders optimizing algorithms and photographers processing massive image libraries," according to Apple.The M5 Max variants are for "those pushing the absolute limits," meaning they're totally overkill for the common laptop user. They start at $3,599 for the 14-inch model and $3,899 for the 16-inch model and come with a base storage of 2TB. Both the M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros also feature Apple's N1 chip for WiFi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. If you want the best of the best when it comes to Apple laptops, these are it. While both models are certainly a pricey investment, the $100 gift card preorder bonus helps to ease a tiny bit of that blow.

The gift card will be automatically added to your cart when you preorder one of Apple’s highest-end laptops available in 14- or 16-inch configurations, and even one of its 14-inch MacBook Pro laptops with the M6 chip. Di Benedetto got a chance to check out the new laptop at Apple’s event, and came away impressed by the Tandem OLED panel’s brightness and contrast, but described the update as “kind of boring” given the relatively small changes to the system otherwise. There are some unique changes to macOS that help make the new touch experience smoother, like magnifying the traffic light-colored buttons on windows when you move your finger near them. The PROLED laptops are also a bit thinner and lighter than standard models, and the Apple logo on the back glows like on older versions. Read our MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display hands-on.

Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple MacBook Pro (M5 Pro) Starting at $2,199 + free $100 gift card Preorder at Best Buy Opens in a new window Credit: Apple Apple MacBook Pro (M5 Max) Starting at $3,599 + free $100 gift card Preorder at Best Buy As you've likely seen by now, Apple had a big week. The company dropped a batch of new products, from the first-ever budget MacBook to an even more powerful MacBook Pro. The latter is pretty darn expensive, but if you lock in a preorder at Best Buy, you'll get a little relief in the form of a free gift card. As of March 5, when you pre-order the new MacBook Pro with either the M5 Pro or M5 Max chip at Best Buy (in any configuration), you'll get a free $100 e-gift card to spend however you please. The laptops will begin shipping on March 11 and you'll receive an email with your free gift once the laptop is in your possession. Sign Me Up By signing up, you agree to receive recurring automated SMS marketing messages from Mashable Deals at the number provided. The new M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros come in two sizes, 14 or 16 inches, and are essentially more powerful versions of the already stellar M5 MacBook Pro. The M5 Pro variants start at $2,199 for the 14-inch laptop and $2,699 for the 16-inch laptop and come with 1TB of base storage. They're built for folks "running complex workflows, like coders optimizing algorithms and photographers processing massive image libraries," according to Apple.The M5 Max variants are for "those pushing the absolute limits," meaning they're totally overkill for the common laptop user. They start at $3,599 for the 14-inch model and $3,899 for the 16-inch model and come with a base storage of 2TB. Both the M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros also feature Apple's N1 chip for WiFi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. If you want the best of the best when it comes to Apple laptops, these are it. While both models are certainly a pricey investment, the $100 gift card preorder bonus helps to ease a tiny bit of that blow.

sources.title: We Tried 7 Popular Salt Vinegar Chips—The Crispiest Brand Took The Top Spot
passages: The best chip is balanced: enough acidity to make your mouth pucker, plenty of salt, a strong potato flavor, and, most importantly, a chip sturdy enough to handle it all.I tried seven popular brands—Lay’s, Siete, Utz, Kettle Brand, Cape Cod, Deep River, and Pringles—to find the one that does salt and vinegar best.
Kettle BrandKettle Brand came extremely close to taking the top spot.

Deep RiverDeep River delivered the first truly satisfying vinegar punch of the group.The acidity hits immediately, but it comes across slightly sweeter and rounder than some of the sharper chips in this ranking.
The vinegar flavor is bright, acidic, and immediately satisfying, with enough salt to make the whole thing pop.My only complaint is how quickly the seasoning disappears.

The first few seconds of each bite are exactly what I want from salt and vinegar, but once that initial tang fades, you’re mostly left with a plain potato chip.Apparently that didn’t bother me too much, because I kept reaching back into the bag.
The vinegar fades quickly, leaving you mostly with the salty potato chip underneath.

The white vinegar gives you that clean acidic bite, while the apple cider vinegar adds a slightly fruitier, more rounded tang that gives the overall flavor more depth.Delish Test Kitchen Manager Alejandro Valdes Lora agreed, praising the great texture and fresh, crisp, slightly oily potato-chip flavor.
Lay’sLay’s were a definite step up for me.The thin chip is light and crispy, and the potato itself tastes better than Utz.
