extraction.body: For generations, most Americans have deposited their money in banks knowing that if somehow things went sideways, their funds would be covered by the full force of the government's treasury. Up to $250,000 in losses are covered through the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), born out of the ashes of the Great Depression. Crypto investors are probably wishing for an FDIC equivalent after Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, was hacked on Oct. 29, with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets. About $3 billion of the stolen assets has been frozen so far, according to a Binance security update. In a security update on Saturday, the exchange said it had replenished 90% of stolen assets and was committed to covering the remaining 10%. Blockchain investigators at TRM Labs and Chainalysis have linked the attack to North Korea , but neither the U.S. government or Binance has publicly confirmed any source for the hack. Understanding how crypto is protected online and what mechanisms exist to serve a role similar to insurance is increasingly important as more Americans invest in cryptocurrency. Roughly one in five U.S. adults say they have invested in, traded, or used crypto , according to Pew Research Center, a figure that is even higher among upper income households (27%). The Securities and Exchange Commission's research from 2024 and 2025 puts that figure closer to 15%, and estimated that roughly 9% of the investing public owned crypto at the time of its survey. Its survey work indicates cryptocurrency ownership is more common for younger individuals, men, and those with higher risk tolerance, but also possessing higher financial literacy. While Binance was making good on its pledge in the aftermath of the hack to cover all losses with its SAFU (Secure Asset Fund for Users) and other company's funds — and that there's no evidence of a wallet private-key leak in this incident — Nikolas Behar, a cybersecurity expert and professor at the University of San Diego, said crypto investors need to understand when using crypto platforms that a pledge is just a pledge "until there's an actual payout." If something happens to your crypto, most consumers are left to navigate a patchwork of options that vary from exchange to exchange and are often very ambiguous. Many exchanges say customers will be paid back if something goes wrong. Josephine Wolff, professor of cybersecurity policy at The Fletcher School at Tufts University, said there "really aren't any legal protections for crypto assets equivalent to FDIC insurance." Customers could try to sue a hacked exchange, she said, for instance by claiming it was negligent, or may recover some funds if the exchange declares bankruptcy, as happened with FTX. But "there's no guarantee of compensation," she said. Michael Tanguma, co-founder and CEO of Onramp Bitcoin, a bitcoin financial services and custody firm, said that when an exchange is hacked, customers are usually repaid, "but only because the exchange decides to pay and has the money to do so." "Nothing in the law requires it to," Tanguma said. "Some stolen funds can be frozen. Tether and Circle, the companies behind the two largest dollar-backed tokens, froze billions of dollars of this week's stolen money, and law enforcement occasionally recovers assets years later," Tanguma said. But he added that bitcoin has no company behind it that can freeze it, so once it leaves your control, it is almost always gone. Customers who lose funds individually are in a very different situation than those caught up in an exchange attack. "When your own account is compromised, through a stolen password, a phishing link, or a hijacked phone number, the outlook is much worse," Tanguma said, noting that exchanges generally treat those losses as the customer's problem, and because crypto transactions are final once confirmed, there is no bank to call and no charge to dispute. Tanguma said keeping coins offline can protect against the kind of attack that hit Binance, though there are other risks associated with this digital security approach. "The stolen funds came from wallets the exchange keeps connected to the internet to process everyday withdrawals, not from its offline reserves," Tanguma said. But he added that the details of this hack point to a larger problem. "Binance says no keys were leaked. The attackers manipulated the system that approves withdrawals, the same approach used in last year's $1.5 billion theft from Bybit, which targeted a transfer out of cold storage," Tanguma said, noting that every custody setup has a weak point, and in most of them it is a single one. "On an exchange, that point is the company: its employees, its approval systems, its finances, and its willingness to repay you," Tanguma said. When you hold your own coins, he said, that point is you: a lost device, a backup found by the wrong person, a tampered device bought from an unofficial seller, a transaction approved under pressure, or a family unable to reach the funds after a death. "Moving savings off an exchange trades one kind of risk for another. It does not remove risk," Tanguma said. Sarah Downey, executive vice president and global blockchain and digital assets advisory leader at Lockton, an insurance brokerage, said other factors also come into play in determining whether you can get your crypto back, including how quickly the theft is discovered, where the funds were moved, whether the exchange or wallet provider has insurance that covers the event, and whether it holds enough reserves to repay customers. "Some companies have set up FDIC-like insurance or other backstops, but whether these pay out depends heavily on the facts of each case. Even without insurance, many exchanges try to repay customers from their own reserves to protect both their customers and their own reputation," Downey said. Crypto exchange reimbursements have followed other security compromises, such as after rogue overseas support agents were bribed to help scam Coinbase customers in May 2025. Bitget, another major exchange, had to tap an in-house fund to reimburse customers after a $388 million hack in September. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said its User Protection Fund, which held more than $464 million, covered the loss. "The Protection Fund was created for moments like this and absorbed the financial impact of the incident," Chen said in a post on X at the time. By comparison, Binance's emergency reserve, the Secure Asset Fund for Users, or SAFU, is estimated at roughly $1 billion to $1.2 billion, and excluding the funds that were frozen, this represented about one-third of the loss. The company said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds and already held more than $5 billion in corresponding token assets. Downey said the steps to take if your crypto is hacked depend on whether investors self-custody or use a third party, such as a regulated exchange. "If they use a third party, they should check that most funds are stored offline or protected with multi-party computation. An investor's own funds should also be stored separately from the exchange's own funds," Downey said, adding that customers should also understand how the custodian authorizes transactions and governs storage. Ryan Reck, founder and principal of Reck Advisory, an independent cybersecurity advisory firm, points to the lack of oversight of crypto. "Crypto has no undo button. Once a transfer confirms, there's no chargeback and no one who can reverse it," Reck said. In some cases, stolen funds can be frozen by an exchange that receives them, or by a stablecoin issuer at a specific blockchain address, but tracing the money and getting it back are two different things. Among the common reasons investors cite for making crypto investments is diversification away from traditional assets, as well as use of crypto as a digital version of gold, investing in the decentralization of finance theme, and betting that as more institutions adopt digital currencies, that will serve as a tailwind. And there's of course also speculation. Today, there are ways to invest in crypto that don't require holding the underlying currency in a wallet, such as exchange-traded funds, including the iShares Bitcoin Trust ( IBIT ), which has over $62 billion in assets, or the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund ( FBTC ), which has over $15 billion in assets. There are also diversified crypto index ETFs holding a basket of top digital currencies, including the Bitwise 10 Crypto Index Fund ( BITW ) and the Grayscale CoinDesk Crypto 5 ETF ( GLDC ). For investors who want to hold crypto directly, Reck says that before trusting any platform, ask four questions:

extraction.body: From the rapidly rising and falling values of Bitcoin to high-profile heists like the hacking of Binance , the world of cryptocurrencies is often in the headlines. The world's biggest crypto exchange said hackers had gained access to $6.3bn (£4.7bn) worth of digital assets, and while it has frozen about half, many remained in the hands of the thieves. These stories are full of specialist language that people outside the industry struggle to understand. So if you're unsure what the blockchain or a crypto echange or even a cryptocurrency itself are, here are some key terms and what they mean. While many may struggle with the finer points of crypto, pretty much everyone has heard of its most famous product: Bitcoin. But what actually is it? Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is to say a type of digital currency. Unlike traditional currencies, Bitcoin is not controlled by centralised financial institutions. This makes it popular for people who think decentralisation can bring financial freedom, but it also makes it extremely volatile with it rising and falling in value at the whim of Bitcoin buyers and sellers. Donald Trump has pledged to make the US the "crypto capital of the world" - backtracking on his previous claim that Bitcoin was a "scam" . Its price topped a much-awaited threshold of $100,000 in December 2024, then rose to $120,000 in July 2025 as US politicians prepared to debate bills to regulate digital assets. In October 2025, Bitcoin hit an all-time high of around $126,000, buoyed by a continued wave of institutional investment and positive market sentiment. But it has been known to plummet in value just as quickly as it spikes. In early February 2026, its price dipped below $65,000 to effectively wipe out gains achieved under President Trump. Against the backdrop of these frequent price fluctuations, speculation continues about the true identity of Bitcoin's mysterious inventor known only as Satoshi Nakamoto. Blockchain is the technology underpinning all cryptocurrencies, and many related products like non-fungible tokens (NFTs). In essence, it is a virtual spreadsheet on which all the buying and selling of crypto is recorded. They are arranged in blocks linked together in a giant chain - hence the name. Every cryptocurrency transaction is individually recorded onto the blockchain by a huge network of volunteers verifying its authenticity by using computer programmes. The incentive to do this for Bitcoin's network is that the first person to validate transactions is rewarded in Bitcoin. This potentially lucrative process, known as mining, is also controversial because of the incredible amount of energy used as people the world over race to be the first to successfully update the blockchain. A crypto exchange is the digital platform where investors can buy, sell and trade cryptocurrencies. Similar to traditional investing, a crypto exchange acts as a brokerage where people can transfer traditional money, like pounds or dollars, in exchange for cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin or Ethereum. Most transactions are accompanied by fees. Binance is the world's biggest, which is part of what makes the hack so monumental. A crypto wallet is a place where investors hold their cryptocurrency. There are two types, a hot wallet and a cold wallet. Cold wallets are physical devices like specially designed USB sticks that store crypto offline typically for safer and longer term storage. Ethereum is used to describe both the second largest cryptocurrency after Bitcoin, represented by the Ether token, and the blockchain underpinning it. This supports an array of different applications and digital assets, such as non-fungible tokens. It functions in a similar way to Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, but in 2022 switched to a greener operating system requiring less computers and energy . ETFs are portfolios that let investors bet on multiple assets without having to buy any themselves. Traded on stock exchanges like shares, their value depends on how the overall portfolio performs in real time. They can comprise a combination of gold and silver bullion, for example, or a mix of shares in both technology and insurance companies. A spot Bitcoin ETF buys the cryptocurrency directly, "on the spot", at its current price, throughout the day. While some ETFs already contained Bitcoin indirectly, the US approved several spot Bitcoin ETFs in January 2024. This allowed new investors, such as investment management firms like Blackrock and Fidelity, to enter the speculative world of Bitcoin without having to worry about digital wallets or navigating crypto exchanges. Meme coins are a form of cryptocurrency used for fun and speculation. But meme coins are heavily criticised for their speculative nature and the risk involved for investors, as they often have little prospect of accumulating value over time. They can also be susceptible to "rug pulls" - where promoters of a cryptocurrency draw in buyers to raise the price of their coin, only to stop trading activity and make off with the money raised from sales. Some celebrities have faced backlash after launching meme coins. Stablecoins themselves are usually controlled by companies that provide them, with transactions recorded on digital ledgers. While held up by some as the future of finance, high profile price collapses of stablecoins have alerted regulators to risks for investors and prompted scrutiny over their supposed stability. XRP is a cryptocurrency used by a platform called the XRP Ledger. It was created by the co-founders of financial services company Ripple Labs in 2012 as a cheaper, faster alternative to Bitcoin. The cryptocurrency has a fixed supply of 100 billion coins, which were created when it launched. Much of it is held by Ripple and periodically released into circulation. Unlike cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, transactions made using XRP are verified through consensus - whereby the majority of validators on its peer-to-peer network must agree whether or not a transaction is valid before it is added to its blockchain. This has been credited with allowing many transactions to take place simultaneously, at high speed and low cost - making it appealing to financial institutions or for processes like cross-border payments. But as with other cryptocurrencies, XRP has received regulatory scrutiny and seen sudden, sharp declines in value . Bridget Devaney turned to the internet with a proposal that sounded equal parts hopeful and improbable - come to Ireland and celebrate the wedding that never happened. The Mexican national, who was living in the US without legal documentation, suffered multiple leg fractures and a hip injury, prosecutors said.

sources.title: From restaurant guides to payments, here’s how TikTok is building a super app
passages: The super app model is big in China with apps like WeChat, which is kind of like Facebook, WhatsApp, Apple Pay, and an app store all rolled into a single platform.
The social media app has steadily expanded its offerings in recent years, adding TikTok Shop, a map for local discovery, more robust search features, games, and more.
TikTok announced this week that it’s adding an in-app restaurant guide , marking another step in the platform’s expansion beyond social media.
The company has also recently been spotted developing a feature that would allow users to send money over direct messages.
TikTok’s potential expansion into payments marks a significant way that the company is branching out beyond a social media platform and into a digital ecosystem.

By aiming to bring financial services into its app, TikTok is looking to increase user engagement, open new revenue streams, and position itself to compete with fintech startups and e-commerce platforms.
Instead of switching between apps, TikTok is working to become the app that people use for most of their digital activities.
After taking its biggest leap with TikTok Shop, the company — which, notably, transitioned to new, primarily U.S. ownership back in January — has applied the same playbook to recent developments.
TikTok has become a popular destination for restaurant recommendations, with viral videos often driving customers to local eateries.
Additionally, Reuters reported in March that TikTok had applied to Brazil’s central bank for approval to operate as a financial technology company offering lending and payment services.

The World Cup hub was made possible through TikTok’s Sports-focused product called “ TikTok GamePlan ,” which is designed to allow sports teams, leagues, and broadcasters to drive discovery and engagement on the platform.
TikTok has launched a robust search experience that surfaces maps, local hashtags, and even reviews to help users discover trending restaurants, travel locations, shops, and local experiences.
TikTok was already eating into Google’s Search business when it first launched, as it quickly surfaced videos featuring commentary and visuals of restaurant food and places.
However, users may still have needed to turn to Google Search to find a place’s exact location or to read reviews.
Over the past few years, however, TikTok has increasingly eliminated that need by integrating detailed information about places right within its app.
It’s worth noting that TikTok first took strides into entertainment with the launch of livestreaming and support for longer videos, a significant move away from its initial focus on 15-second videos.
The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps.
It also reflects how the app is expanding its role in users’ everyday decisions, from what they buy to where they choose to go out to eat.
In early June, the company launched a dedicated hub for the FIFA World Cup where users can see scores, match schedules, standings, trending videos, highlights, videos from players, and more.
TikTok GO surfaces lodging and things to do through videos, search, and location pages.
When users find something they’re interested in, they can view details, check availability, and complete a booking.

Instead of directing users to third-party websites after they find a destination or recommendation in a video, TikTok has started positioning itself as a one-stop platform where viral travel content can drive bookings and revenue.
The company said it would focus on driving music listening and continue partnering with music streaming services rather than competing with them.
If people are already watching videos on TikTok but want to keep up with the score, they can do so without leaving the app or opening a dedicated sports news app or Google.

TikTok announced this week that it’s adding an in-app restaurant guide , marking another step in the platform’s expansion beyond social media. The company has also recently been spotted developing a feature that would allow users to send money over direct messages. The social media app has steadily expanded its offerings in recent years, adding TikTok Shop, a map for local discovery, more robust search features, games, and more. It appears that TikTok is taking steps to evolve into a “super app,” a single platform where users can do much more than just watch and share videos and that can actually handle a wide range of needs in one destination. The super app model is big in China with apps like WeChat, which is kind of like Facebook, WhatsApp, Apple Pay, and an app store all rolled into a single platform. Of course, there’s the question of whether a super app model would work outside of China, but that doesn’t mean TikTok won’t try. Instead of switching between apps, TikTok is working to become the app that people use for most of their digital activities. After taking its biggest leap with TikTok Shop, the company — which, notably, transitioned to new, primarily U.S. ownership back in January — has applied the same playbook to recent developments. TikTok has become a popular destination for restaurant recommendations, with viral videos often driving customers to local eateries. Now, the platform is looking to make that discovery process even easier with a new feature called “ Must Eat .” The community-driven guide highlights restaurants getting attention on the platform. “Must Eat” draws on more than 40 million posts and comments to compile restaurant recommendations and curated lists in one place. Users can browse restaurants by city and narrow their search by cuisine, price, rating, and location. The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps. It also reflects how the app is expanding its role in users’ everyday decisions, from what they buy to where they choose to go out to eat. Bloomberg reported in August that TikTok is developing a feature that would allow users to send each other money via direct messages. If rolled out, the feature would use the social media service’s TikTok Pay offering, which is already available in Southeast Asia for TikTok Shop purchases. Additionally, Reuters reported in March that TikTok had applied to Brazil’s central bank for approval to operate as a financial technology company offering lending and payment services. TikTok’s potential expansion into payments marks a significant way that the company is branching out beyond a social media platform and into a digital ecosystem. By aiming to bring financial services into its app, TikTok is looking to increase user engagement, open new revenue streams, and position itself to compete with fintech startups and e-commerce platforms. Over the years, TikTok has steadily been looking to become a place where users can come for sports highlights and content. In early June, the company launched a dedicated hub for the FIFA World Cup where users can see scores, match schedules, standings, trending videos, highlights, videos from players, and more. If people are already watching videos on TikTok but want to keep up with the score, they can do so without leaving the app or opening a dedicated sports news app or Google. The World Cup hub was made possible through TikTok’s Sports-focused product called “ TikTok GamePlan ,” which is designed to allow sports teams, leagues, and broadcasters to drive discovery and engagement on the platform. The social media giant also has partnerships with Major League Soccer (MLS) and Major League Baseball (MLB) for behind-the-scenes and exclusive content. In May, TikTok launched TikTok GO , a way for users to discover and book hotels, attractions, and experiences directly within its app in the United States. TikTok GO surfaces lodging and things to do through videos, search, and location pages. When users find something they’re interested in, they can view details, check availability, and complete a booking. Instead of directing users to third-party websites after they find a destination or recommendation in a video, TikTok has started positioning itself as a one-stop platform where viral travel content can drive bookings and revenue. While people have already been using TikTok as a search engine and replacement for Google, this latest step puts TikTok in more direct competition with Google’s core businesses, Search and Google Maps, because it’s working to not only be the app where you discover places, but also the platform where you purchase that trip. It’s widely known that one of TikTok’s biggest leaps beyond social media was the launch of TikTok Shop. TikTok began testing TikTok Shop in 2021 and launched it in the U.S. in 2023. Since then, the company has been able to successfully compete with Amazon, Shein, and other online marketplaces. According to eMarketer, TikTok Shop grew its U.S. sales by 407% in 2024 and another 108% in 2025 to reach $15.82 billion. As of last year, the company accounted for 18.2% of total social commerce in the U.S., with that number expected to reach 24.1% by 2027. Additionally, TikTok began challenging digital marketplaces even further with the launch of TikTok Shop gift cards late last year. TikTok Shop has also recently expanded into luxury retail , after initially mainly being known for cheap goods. TikTok’s popularity has influenced the music industry and how people discover new music, and the company tried to capitalize on this by launching a streaming service called TikTok Music in 2023 to take on platforms like Spotify and Apple Music, but ended up shutting it down a year later. The company said it would focus on driving music listening and continue partnering with music streaming services rather than competing with them. TikTok hasn’t completely abandoned its music ambitions, however, as the company recently introduced a feature that lets Apple Music subscribers play full songs in the app after discovering them on their “For You” feed. TikTok has launched a robust search experience that surfaces maps, local hashtags, and even reviews to help users discover trending restaurants, travel locations, shops, and local experiences. It has also added more detailed information about places and restaurants on dedicated pages, allowing users to quickly see things like opening hours, star ratings, price ranges, and more. TikTok was already eating into Google’s Search business when it first launched, as it quickly surfaced videos featuring commentary and visuals of restaurant food and places. However, users may still have needed to turn to Google Search to find a place’s exact location or to read reviews. Over the past few years, however, TikTok has increasingly eliminated that need by integrating detailed information about places right within its app. While TikTok is known for user-generated entertainment, the company has also begun embracing microdramas by launching an in-app Minis section and a dedicated stand-alone app for bite-sized TV shows that can be watched in a series of one-minute episodes. While TikTok already competes with streaming giants like Netflix for users’ attention, its move into scripted shows puts it in even more direct competition with them. It’s worth noting that TikTok first took strides into entertainment with the launch of livestreaming and support for longer videos, a significant move away from its initial focus on 15-second videos. TikTok has also launched a series of casual games in its app to get users to spend even more time on its platform and engage with others in DMs. The addition of games marked TikTok’s ongoing effort to go from a social media platform to an all-in-one entertainment platform where you can not only scroll through videos, but also challenge friends to easy-to-play games.

extraction.body: Vic Mensa is one of those people who has done so many things that it’s hard to remember where you were first introduced to him. Or maybe his house-influenced single “Down On My Luck”? Maybe you didn’t even realize that Mensa was a rapper. Or perhaps you’re mostly aware of him through his activism, social media presence (peeling oranges and waxing poetic), or his podcast The Vic Mensa Show. Part of the secret to being so prolific, it turns out, is Voice Memos. Songs, essay ideas, orange tree thoughts, voice notes to myself at some wild hour, little things my son says that I do not want to lose. My phone is a million distractions in one rectangle, but Voice Memos is one of the few parts of it that still feels honest. That’s definitely where my voice has really found its legs. I started out peeling an orange and talking through whatever was on my mind, and it turned into this whole conversation with people about politics, history, music, grief, jokes, fatherhood, all of it. That response helped show me there was room for The Vic Mensa Show too. What is the last GIF or meme you used? [Image: Ummm… that is not Vic Mensa.

sources.title: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia
passages: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday .
Anthropic has signed a $44.6 billion contract for the project’s first building alone, according to Nscale’s IPO filing .

In essence, the chipmaker would be co-signing a customer’s loans, a sign of how hard the AI industry is working to keep its buildout plans afloat as investors grow jittery about the amounts of money involved.
Anthropic’s contract with Nscale covers the first 460-megawatt building at Nscale’s West Virginia campus, which is expected to use Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips.
The companies are also discussing a second deal worth roughly $45 billion for another building.

Under what’s known as a residual value guarantee, Nvidia would step in if Nscale defaulted on construction payments, temporarily take over the facility, and help find a buyer and new tenant, according to The Information .
Nscale has struggled to get its projects off the ground.
The company had about 25,000 advanced AI chips running in August , a fraction of the nearly 500,000 it plans to deploy.
Runoff from the construction site has flooded nearby homes more than once .
In September, after months of negotiations , the project won state certification.
The stakes are high for Nscale, which is seeking to go public at a valuation of up to $35 billion despite growing concerns about its ability to deliver on ambitious data center projects.
That includes $1 billion in convertible financing committed to Nscale in September.
Anthropic, one of the largest buyers of AI computing power, has spread its infrastructure spending across multiple chipmakers.
Nvidia’s earlier support for cloud providers has mostly covered leases and chip purchases, not construction.
This month, Microsoft pulled out of a planned Nscale site in England after grid power for it was pushed into the 2030s.

extraction.body: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday . Bloomberg later corroborated the report. Anthropic has signed a $44.6 billion contract for the project’s first building alone, according to Nscale’s IPO filing . In essence, the chipmaker would be co-signing a customer’s loans, a sign of how hard the AI industry is working to keep its buildout plans afloat as investors grow jittery about the amounts of money involved. The proposed arrangement would help Nscale secure financing for the electricity and construction costs of its West Virginia campus. Under what’s known as a residual value guarantee, Nvidia would step in if Nscale defaulted on construction payments, temporarily take over the facility, and help find a buyer and new tenant, according to The Information . Nvidia’s earlier support for cloud providers has mostly covered leases and chip purchases, not construction. The stakes are high for Nscale, which is seeking to go public at a valuation of up to $35 billion despite growing concerns about its ability to deliver on ambitious data center projects. Anthropic’s contract with Nscale covers the first 460-megawatt building at Nscale’s West Virginia campus, which is expected to use Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips. The companies are also discussing a second deal worth roughly $45 billion for another building. Nscale has struggled to get its projects off the ground. The company had about 25,000 advanced AI chips running in August , a fraction of the nearly 500,000 it plans to deploy. Its West Virginia campus has run into trouble of its own. Runoff from the construction site has flooded nearby homes more than once . In September, after months of negotiations , the project won state certification. This month, Microsoft pulled out of a planned Nscale site in England after grid power for it was pushed into the 2030s. Nvidia has been a major financial backer of the sector, extending roughly $170 billion in investments and credit support to neoclouds and large customers, according to The Information. That includes $1 billion in convertible financing committed to Nscale in September. Neoclouds, which rent out AI computing power without a cash-rich core business behind them, have come under pressure from investors. Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN had each fallen more than 30% in October as of last week, CNBC reported . The proposed guarantee would deepen Nvidia’s financial ties to Nscale while helping secure a major customer for its chips. Anthropic, one of the largest buyers of AI computing power, has spread its infrastructure spending across multiple chipmakers. One investor told The Information that Anthropic’s involvement likely explains Nvidia’s interest in keeping Nscale’s project on track. The discussions also come as Anthropic faces questions about how it will finance its own rapid expansion. The company filed to go public this week, but Blackstone has warned investors that Anthropic may receive a below-investment-grade credit rating after its IPO. A junk rating would raise Anthropic’s borrowing costs and could push it to keep relying on stronger partners to back its debt.
